title: I'm vibing a gladiator management game!
author: StarDrifterG
selftext:
Hello

I've been building City of Gladiators, a free browser based gladiator management game!

[https://stardrifterg.itch.io/city-of-gladiators](https://stardrifterg.itch.io/city-of-gladiators)

or

[https://city-of-gladiators.com/](https://city-of-gladiators.com/)

I'd love some feedback! Is the gameplay easy to understand? Does the progression feel too slow or too difficult?

Thanks for checking it out!

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body:
Hey u/StarDrifterG, this falls under Rule 4. Commercial posts are okay here, but you need to talk about how it was developed using AI, so the community has something to discuss. This post doesn't have enough on that yet.

To keep it up, edit your post or reply to this comment within an hour with some details on your dev process, like:

- which AI tools you used, and what for
- how they fit into your workflow
- problems you hit and how you dealt with them

"Made with AI", a list of tools or a ChatGPT bullet list won't cut it. If nothing's added by then, this post may be removed.

If you think we got this wrong, [message the mods](https://www.reddit.com/message/compose?to=/r/aigamedev).

comments.author: protheus99
comments.body:
I recommend you going back to the crates and looking at some of the older rome type games - Centurion Defender of Rome is a good example, it had this great gladiator mini game you can get inspiration from. 

Overall i enjoyed your game and to think it's very fun, thank you for sharing
